subtopics.title: Cost Price, Selling Price and Percentage Profit

questions.question: Ingredients of R150, R250, R50 and R30 for a batch of 80 boerewors rolls give a cost price per roll of:
Selling at R10 with a cost price of R6,00, the percentage profit on cost is:
The selling price is best described as:
options: A number fixed by the ingredients
A decision steered by cost price, competitors' prices and what customers will pay

questions.question: Takings of R9 180 this season against R8 500 last season is an increase of:

subtopics.title: Break-even: Where Loss Turns into Profit

questions.question: The R290 site fee is a fixed cost because:
options: It is spent before the first customer and does not change with the number sold
It increases with every roll made

questions.question: Each roll sold at R10 with variable cost R6,00 contributes toward the fixed cost:
The break-even number of rolls is 290 ÷ 4,00 = 72,5, reported as:
options: 73 — at 72 the stall is still R2 short, at 73 it is R2 ahead

questions.question: On the break-even graph, the loss at a quantity left of the crossing appears as:
options: The slope of the income line
The point where the cost line starts
The horizontal distance between the lines
The vertical gap where the cost line rides above the income line

subtopics.title: Interest and Banking, Year by Year

questions.question: R8 000 in a fixed deposit at 6% compound grows in year one to:
Year two's interest is R508,80, larger than year one's R480, because:
options: The 6% now works on the grown balance of R8 480 — interest earning interest

questions.question: After three years, compound at 6% gives R9 528,13 against simple interest's R9 440 — a difference of:
A credit card differs from a debit card because credit:
options: Spends the bank's money, which must be repaid — with interest if late

subtopics.title: Inflation: When the Same Trolley Costs More

questions.question: At 5% inflation, an ingredient basket of R2 400 costs next year:
Milk rising from R22,50 to R24,30 is an inflation rate of:
options: 8% — the increase of 1,80 divided by the OLD price of 22,50

questions.question: Two years of 5% inflation multiplies prices by:
options: 1,05 × 1,05 = 1,1025, because the second rise stands on the first

questions.question: Savings earning nothing while inflation runs at 5%:
options: Are unaffected, since the rand amount is unchanged
Lose about 5% of their buying power each year

questions.question: The cost price of R6,00 is called the floor because:
options: Selling below it makes every sale dig the hole deeper
It is the lowest price competitors charge
Prices cannot legally go below it

questions.question: Measured against cost, the R4,00 profit is 66,7%; measured against the selling price it would be 40%. The expected answer is:
options: Profit on COST, with the base written next to the answer

questions.question: The budget projected R550 for ingredients and the till slip says R480. The one-sentence analysis is:
options: The projection was wrong so the budget fails
R70 under budget, because the boerewors was on special

subtopics.title: How Many Before We Stop Losing

questions.question: At eight in the morning, before any sales, the stall is already R290 down because:
options: The site fee is paid whether the day goes well or badly

questions.question: The 73rd roll is special because:
options: It tips the stall from loss into profit — before it sales shrink the loss, after it each sale is full profit
It is the last of the batch

questions.question: In the race picture of the graph, income catches cost because:
options: Income climbs R10 a step against cost's R6,00, despite cost's R290 head start

questions.question: Raising the price from R10 to R10,50 moves break-even from 73 to:
options: 65 — each sale now pushes R4,50 against the R290

subtopics.title: The Bank's Staircase and the Trolley That Grows

questions.question: The bank staircase's steps get taller each year because:
options: Interest starts earning its own interest
The bank raises the rate annually

questions.question: The staircase's dark twin is:
options: A debt at compound interest climbing the same steps when nothing is repaid

questions.question: Finding an inflation rate from two prices always divides by:
options: The OLD price — milk from R22,50 to R24,30 is 1,80 over 22,50, eight percent

questions.question: Money earning 6% while prices climb 5% is truly growing by:
options: Only the sliver between the two rates
